I couldn't write the commentary notes. My research tool stopped working before I could read any sources, so I don't have any material from the approved sites. I can't make notes from memory because of your rules: only report what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge.

These are the pages I tried to load, and the ones I'd start with next time:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-115/
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/115.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/115.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/115.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/psalms/115.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/mhcw/psalms/115.htm (Matthew Henry)
  - preceptaustin.org/psalm-115-commentary
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** newadvent.org/fathers/1801115.htm. This is Augustine's exposition. The Latin Bible joins Psalms 114 and 115 into one psalm, so this one may appear as the second half of his Psalm 113.
- **Still to search:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on Psalm 115 (spurgeon.org), the NET Bible notes on Psalm 115 (netbible.org), and the tradition-specific sites. The likeliest places for the traditions to differ are verses 1, 3, 8 and 17.

If you send the request again in a new message, the tool should be available. I'll then read these pages and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for every point.
